questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question:
Consider the translation scheme shown below.

  • $S \rightarrow T\;R$
  • $R \rightarrow + T \{\text{print}(‘+’);\} R\mid \varepsilon$
  • $T  \rightarrow$ num $\{\text{print}$(num.val)$;\}$

Here num is a token that represents an integer and num.val represents the corresponding integer value. For an input string ‘$9 + 5 + 2$’, this translation scheme will print
questions.rawQuestionHtml:
Consider the translation scheme shown below.

  • $S \rightarrow T\;R$
  • $R \rightarrow + T \{\text{print}(‘+’);\} R\mid \varepsilon$
  • $T  \rightarrow$ num $\{\text{print}$(num.val)$;\}$

Here num is a token that represents an integer and num.val represents the corresponding integer value. For an input string ‘$9 + 5 + 2$’, this translation scheme will print

  1. $9 + 5 + 2$
  2. $9 \ 5 + 2 +$
  3. $9 \ 5 \ 2 + +$
  4. $+ + 9 \ 5 \ 2$

questions.title: GATE EE 2021 | GA Question: 3
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question: A program consists of two modules executed sequentially. Let $f_1(t)$ and $f_2(t)$ respectively denote the probability density functions of time taken to execute the two modules. The probability density function of the overall time taken to execute the program is given by
questions.rawQuestionHtml:
A program consists of two modules executed sequentially. Let $f_1(t)$ and $f_2(t)$ respectively denote the probability density functions of time taken to execute the two modules. The probability density function of the overall time taken to execute the program is given by 

  1. $f_1(t)+f_2(t)$

  2. $\int_0^t f_1(x)f_2(x)dx$

  3. $\int_0^t f_1(x)f_2(t-x)dx$

  4. $\max\{f_1(t),f_2(t)\}$

questions.title: GATE EE 2021 | GA Question: 4
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question:
Consider three IP networks $A, B$ and $C$. Host $H_A$ in network $A$ sends messages each containing $180$ bytes of application data to a host $H_C$ in network $C$. The $\text{TCP}$ layer prefixes $20$ byte header to the message.

This passes through an intermediate network $B$.The maximum packet size, including $20$ byte IP header, in each network is:

The network $A$ and $B$ are connected through a $1$ Mbps link, while $B$ and $C$
 are connected by a $512$ Kbps link (bps = bits per second).        

Assuming that the packets are correctly delivered, how many bytes, including headers, are delivered to the $IP$ layer at the destination for one application message, in the best case? Consider only data packets.

This passes through an intermediate network $B$.The maximum packet size, including $20$ byte IP header, in each network is:

  • A: $\text{1000 bytes}$

The network $A$ and $B$ are connected through a $1$ Mbps link, while $B$ and $C$

questions.title: GATE EE 2021 | GA Question: 10
questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question:
Consider a three word machine instruction

$\text{ADD} A[R_0], @B$

The first operand (destination) $“A[R_0]”$ uses indexed addressing mode with $R_0$ as the index register. The second operand (source) $“@B”$ uses indirect addressing mode. $A$ and $B$ are memory addresses residing at the second and third words, respectively. The first word of the instruction specifies the opcode, the index register designation and the source and destination addressing modes. During execution of $\text{ADD}$ instruction, the two operands are added and stored in the destination (first operand).

The number of memory cycles needed during the execution cycle of the instruction is:
questions.rawQuestionHtml:

During execution of $\text{ADD}$ instruction, the two operands are added and stored in the destination (first operand).

questions.title: GATE EE 2021 | EE Question: 1
questions.subject: Power Electronics & Drives
questions.question: A DC-DC step-down (buck) converter has an input voltage of $48\text{ V}$ and duty cycle $D = 0.25$. Under continuous conduction mode, the steady-state average output voltage is:
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Power Electronics & Drives):

For a buck converter, $V_o = D \cdot V_s = 0.25 \times 48\text{ V} = 12\text{ V}$.

questions.title: GATE EE 2021 | EE Question: 6
questions.subject: Electrical & Electronic Measurements
questions.question: A Permanent Magnet Moving Coil (PMMC) instrument responds strictly to:
options: The true average (DC) value of current
The Root Mean Square (RMS) value of current

structuredOptions.label: A
structuredOptions.text: The true average (DC) value of current
structuredOptions.html: The true average (DC) value of current

structuredOptions.label: B
structuredOptions.text: The Root Mean Square (RMS) value of current
structuredOptions.html: The Root Mean Square (RMS) value of current

questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Electrical & Electronic Measurements):

Because deflecting torque in PMMC is proportional to instantaneous current ($T_d = BINA$), over an AC cycle the net torque averages out to zero. Hence it strictly registers the average (DC) component.

questions.subject: Electromagnetic Fields
questions.question: Maxwell's divergence equation $\nabla \cdot \vec{B} = 0$ physically asserts that:
options: Isolated magnetic monopoles do not exist in nature
Electric field is conservative in static conditions

questions.title: GATE EE 2021 | EE Question: 26
questions.subject: Power Electronics & Drives
questions.question: A single-phase full-wave controlled bridge rectifier is fed from a $230\text{ V}$ (RMS), $50\text{ Hz}$ AC source. The firing angle is $\alpha = 60^\circ$. Assuming continuous conduction, the average DC output voltage $V_{dc} = \frac{2 V_m}{\pi} \cos \alpha$ (in Volts) is ________ (round off to one decimal place).
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Power Electronics & Drives):

$V_m = 230 \times \sqrt{2} = 325.27\text{ V}$. $V_{dc} = \frac{2 V_m}{\pi} \cos(60^\circ) = \frac{2 \times 325.27}{\pi} \times 0.5 = \frac{325.27}{3.1416} = 103.54\text{ V}$.

questions.title: GATE EE 2021 | EE Question: 32
questions.subject: Analog & Digital Electronics
questions.question: An ideal op-amp in inverting amplifier configuration has input resistance $R_1 = 10\,\text{k}\Omega$ and feedback resistance $R_f = 100\,\text{k}\Omega$. If input voltage is $V_{\text{in}} = 0.5\text{ V}$, the output voltage $V_{\text{out}} = -\frac{R_f}{R_1} V_{\text{in}}$ (in Volts) is ________.
questions.explanation:
Step-by-Step Solution (Analog & Digital Electronics):

Inverting voltage gain $A_v = -\frac{R_f}{R_1} = -\frac{100}{10} = -10$. Output $V_{\text{out}} = -10 \times 0.5\text{ V} = -5.0\text{ V}$.

questions.rawQuestionHtml:
If the cube roots of unity are $1, \omega$ and $\omega^2$, then the roots of the following equation are $$(x-1)^3 +8 =0$$

  1. $-1, 1 + 2\omega, 1 + 2\omega^2$   
  2. $1, 1 - 2\omega, 1 - 2\omega^2$
  3. $-1, 1 - 2\omega, 1 - 2\omega^2$
  4. $-1, 1 + 2\omega, -1 + 2\omega^2$
